desc: Derive the fixed-k reduction: each letter ends with 0 or k copies; only adjacent one-step changes i->i+1 give a saving of min(surplus_i, deficit_{i+1}); multi-step changes never beat delete+insert.
Implement the two-state DP over letters a..z for k from 1 to n, returning min cost.

Validate: asserted the three provided examples give 1, 0, 2; brute-force BFS over count vectors for lengths 3..7 across {a,b,c}, {a,b,c,d}, {a,b,c,z}, {a,b,d} reported 0 mismatches (~50k strings); extra=2 vs extra=3 alphabet check confirmed alphabet sufficiency.
Time the DP on worst cases (s='a'*20000 and a mixed 20000-length string); both complete well under a second.
No mismatches appeared, so the adjacent-only reduction is confirmed and no fallback (min-cost-flow / transportation DP) is needed.
